iterations.explanation: Dimensions separate access, data protection, payments, monitoring, event propagation, and scheduling; values and relations capture variation, security constraints, lifecycle dependencies.

clusters.name: Authentication and Access Control
clusters.description: Authentication and account-access decisions, distinguished by credential methods and controls governing verification, transmission, storage, and time-limited access tokens.

relations.rationale: Credential-based authentication requires corresponding protections for credentials and verification data throughout their lifecycle.

values.label: Email/password authentication
values.description: Users authenticate through email and password credentials rather than SSO or passwordless methods.

values.label: Thirty-minute verification-code expiration
values.description: Verification codes expire after 30 minutes, limiting the window for account-verification misuse.

clusters.name: Data Protection and Encryption
clusters.description: Protection of personal and payment-related information through encryption and secure handling across transmission, storage, registration, and sensitive operations.

relations.rationale: Privacy and security requirements constrain authentication and payment designs by requiring protection of credentials and sensitive financial data.
Encryption and secure data handling restrict which external payment-integration designs are acceptable for GDPR and related compliance obligations.

values.label: End-to-end encryption across the data lifecycle
values.description: User data is encrypted end to end, including data in transit and at rest, with heightened protection for registration and sensitive operations.

clusters.name: Payment Integration Abstraction
clusters.description: External payment-provider integration decisions, distinguished by abstraction boundaries that isolate CityBike from provider-specific APIs and processing behavior.

relations.rationale: Payment integration must satisfy data-protection requirements when handling payment information through external providers.

values.label: Adapter-based provider API abstraction
values.description: Provider-specific APIs are normalized behind adapter components and a dedicated integration layer.

values.label: Payment facade with processor delegation
values.description: A payment facade exposes simple methods while delegating provider-specific processing internally.

clusters.name: Operational Monitoring and Reporting
clusters.description: Operational visibility decisions, distinguished by how bike status, usage information, and reporting outputs are consolidated for dashboards and administrators.

relations.rationale: Monitoring dashboards depend on timely status propagation so operational views remain synchronized with current bike conditions.

values.label: Aggregated real-time operations dashboard
values.description: A dashboard aggregates real-time bike status, usage data, and reporting outputs for operational oversight.

clusters.name: Bike Status Event Propagation
clusters.description: Bike-state communication decisions, distinguished by mechanisms that propagate live status changes to dashboards, monitoring components, or other subscribers.

relations.rationale: Publishing status changes produces the timely updates required by operational monitoring and reporting consumers.

values.label: Observer-based real-time status propagation
values.description: An Observer-based mechanism pushes bike status changes to dashboard and monitoring subscribers in real time.

clusters.name: Rental Lifecycle Scheduling
clusters.description: Rental lifecycle timing decisions, distinguished by tracking rental durations and scheduling rider notifications around expiry events.

values.label: Scheduled pre-expiry rental notifications
values.description: A scheduler tracks rental duration and sends notifications before the rental expires.

clusters.name: Real-Time Event and Notification Propagation
clusters.description: Event and notification propagation choices, distinguished by observer-based delivery of bike, rental, availability, and user-facing state changes.

relations.rationale: Publishing status and rental changes produces timely updates required by operational monitoring, availability views, and user interfaces.

values.label: Observer-based real-time status propagation
values.description: An Observer-based mechanism pushes bike status changes to dashboard and monitoring subscribers in real time.

values.label: Observer-based user notifications
values.description: The Observer pattern notifies riders about bike status changes and usage-history availability.

values.label: Observer-based bike availability synchronization

values.label: Observer-driven rental and UI state updates

clusters.name: Rental Lifecycle Scheduling
clusters.description: Rental timing choices, distinguished by scheduling mechanisms for duration tracking, expiry handling, reminders, and pre-expiry notifications.

relations.rationale: Rental lifecycle state transitions identify the time-dependent conditions that scheduling mechanisms must monitor and trigger.

values.label: Scheduled pre-expiry rental notifications
values.description: A scheduler tracks rental duration and sends notifications before the rental expires.

clusters.name: Rental Operation Encapsulation
clusters.description: Behavioral encapsulation choices for rental operations, distinguished by packaging rider actions as commands and separating notifications from command execution.

relations.rationale: Excluding notifications from command abstractions establishes a boundary that constrains how rental events and user notifications are propagated.

values.label: Command-based rental operation encapsulation
values.description: The Command pattern packages ride-rental actions as commands while keeping notifications outside the behavioral command abstraction.

clusters.name: Rental Lifecycle State Modeling
clusters.description: Rental lifecycle state-modeling choices, distinguished by explicit state-transition representations for managing rental behavior over time.

relations.rationale: Explicit rental states provide the lifecycle conditions needed to determine when scheduled reminders or expiry actions apply.

values.label: State pattern for rental lifecycle
values.description: The State pattern models transitions and behavior across the bike rental lifecycle.

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already absorbed by the existing taxonomy. The monitoring/dashboard items fit Dimension 4 (Operational Monitoring and Reporting) and Dimension 5 (Bike Status Event Propagation). Password-based authentication, verification-code expiration, secure transmission, secure storage, end-to-end encryption, and secure registration all fall under Dimension 1 (Authentication and Access Control) and Dimension 2 (Data Protection and Encryption). The payment abstraction and adapter/facade/delegation codes are captured by Dimension 3 (Payment Integration Abstraction). The rental duration and pre-expiry notification codes are covered by Dimension 6 (Rental Lifecycle Scheduling). No open code introduces a genuinely new architectural concern beyond the current orthogonal dimensions for the CityBike use case.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. The authentication-related codes map to Dimension 1 (verification-code generation, delivery, 30-minute TTL expiration, TTL-based expiry mechanism, biometric thumbprint authentication) and Dimension 2 (immediate biometric data deletion after verification). The command/notification boundary is covered by Dimension 7 and its relation to Dimension 5, while the event propagation, availability synchronization, and UI update codes are captured by Dimension 5’s observer-based real-time propagation variants. The rental lifecycle modeling and scheduler-driven timing notifications are covered by Dimensions 8 and 6, respectively. No open code introduces a distinct architectural concern outside these existing axes for the CityBike use case.
